title: Probation Prep Pack
description: The composite playbook for the final 21 days of a Scrum Master's probation. Four sub-artefacts. The SM probation pack is structurally similar to the PM version but the evidence base is different — the SM is being assessed on whether they hold the room, not whether they hit the date. The worked conversation example is the Maya-tier signature artefact: turn-by-turn editorial commentary on what each line of an actual review conversation is doing.

# Probation Prep Pack — Scrum Master
_Four sub-artefacts. Self-assessment first, pre-review 1:1 second, evidence portfolio third, conversation playbook fourth (rehearse last)._

## Sub-artefact 1: Self-Assessment

One page. Three columns. Filled in honestly.

| Held | Learned | Want next |
|------|---------|-----------|
_'Held' instead of 'delivered' — the SM's job is holding the space. Three to five items in each column. Specific._

## Sub-artefact 2: Pre-Review 1:1 Agenda

Thirty minutes, booked a week before the formal review. Framing:

> 'I want to be ready for our review. Can we talk about what good looks like for a Scrum Master in this team — both how you'd describe it now and how you'd describe it in a year?'

The two-horizon question is the difference between a PM's pre-review and an SM's. SMs are assessed on trajectory more than on delivery; the question pulls trajectory into the conversation.

### Agenda

1. **My read of how the team has worked over 90 days** (3 minutes). One paragraph.
2. **What I held well and what was hard to hold** (5 minutes).
3. **Your read of what I held** (15 minutes). Listen.
4. **What 'a good SM here in a year' looks like** (5 minutes). Ask explicitly.
5. **What you'd like me to bring to the formal review** (2 minutes).

## Sub-artefact 3: Evidence Portfolio

_Not a list of impediments closed. A list of moments held. Three to five._

| Moment | Date | What was at stake | What changed because of how it was held |
|--------|------|-------------------|----------------------------------------|
|        |      |                   |                                        |

_The 'what was at stake' column is the discipline. An SM's value lives in the things that didn't happen because of them. A team member who didn't leave. A blow-up retro that didn't blow up. A PO conversation that prevented next sprint's chaos. Make the invisible visible._

## Sub-artefact 4: The Conversation Playbook

_See the annotated worked example below._

worked_examples.content_md:
# The Scrum Master Probation Review — Worked Example

_Setting: Adisa Okafor (Head of Delivery, hiring manager) and the SM. Day 87. Thirty minutes. The team likes the SM. The question is whether the SM's style scales to a harder team._

---

**Adisa:** So the team likes you. But I want to know if you can hold a harder room.

_[**SM's silent thought:** This is not the 'how did it go' question I rehearsed. This is the actual conversation. Don't list achievements; answer the question being asked.]_

**SM:** The hardest single room I've held was the retro in week 9, when Naledi cried.

_[**Annotation:** Names a specific moment as the lead. Doesn't open with the impediment-log metric (which is real but is the safe answer). Goes to the harder thing first — Adisa will trust this answer more.]_

**Adisa:** Talk me through it.

**SM:** I knew the room was tired going in. The compliance project had gone over and Naledi had carried it. I'd planned a timeline retro because I wanted the team to see the dips. Naledi spoke last in the opening round and started to cry. I held the silence for about fifteen seconds. I think I said 'take your time, we're not in a hurry'. She gathered herself in maybe thirty seconds. The conversation we then had was the one the team needed to have about workload over that month.

_[**Annotation:** Specifics. Not 'I held the space' (abstract) — 'I held the silence for about fifteen seconds; I think I said "take your time, we're not in a hurry"' (behavioural). Adisa can see what the SM actually did.]_

**Adisa:** What did you not do?

_[**SM's silent thought:** The question is testing whether I know the negative space — what the wrong move would have been. This is the harder one.]_

**SM:** I didn't suggest a break. That was the move I felt pulled to — give her the bathroom exit. I think if I'd done that we'd have got a tidier meeting and lost the real conversation. I also didn't go to her afterwards to 'check in' in a way that would have made it a thing. I let her come to me; she did, three days later.

_[**Annotation:** Names the move not made. The decision-not-made is the SM's actual work — most of the value is in restraint. Adisa is testing whether the SM can see that.]_

**Adisa:** And the impediment-log work — your median resolution dropped from 8 days to 5. How real is that number?

**SM:** It's real but it's not the thing I'd want to be measured on alone. About two-thirds of the improvement was learning the org chart — who specifically owns what. That's a learning curve any SM moves through in their first quarter; it'll plateau. The other third was raising impediments earlier, when they feel like 'something to keep an eye on' rather than waiting until they're actively blocking. That's the part I'd want to keep getting better at.

_[**Annotation:** Receives a positive metric without over-claiming. Distinguishes one-time gains from ongoing improvement. Adisa will trust this — the SM understands what their number actually means.]_

**Adisa:** What about Hari?

_[**SM's silent thought:** Hari is the PO. The team finds him hard. Adisa is asking whether I've started the PO-coaching work or whether I've been working around him.]_

**SM:** The wishlist conversation in week 7. I had to find him after planning because he'd already left. I framed it as 'how do we frame commitment in planning' rather than 'eleven stories is too many'. He told on himself in the first three minutes — said he just needed to see the team leaning in. We landed on six commit + five stretch from there. The harder thing is that the same conversation has happened twice since, just in slightly different forms. I think we need a different shape — maybe a monthly 'how we work together' session that's not tied to a single planning meeting. I haven't done it yet.

_[**Annotation:** Names what the SM has done (the week-7 conversation), what hasn't yet worked permanently (the recurrence), and what they think the next move is (a different cadence). Honest about the gap. Doesn't oversell the win.]_

**Adisa:** OK. So — there's a team coming up in six months — the platform group. Their SM is leaving. They've chewed through two SMs in two years. I'm thinking about who could take it.

_[**SM's silent thought:** This is the question. The wrong answers are 'yes please' (over-eager) and 'I'm not sure I'm ready' (under-confident). The right answer is somewhere specific in between.]_

**SM:** I'd want it. I'd also want to shadow Saara for six weeks first if you could land that — partly to learn the team, partly because I haven't yet had to come into a room that didn't want me there. That's the gap.

_[**Annotation:** 'I'd want it.' (Confident.) 'I'd also want to shadow Saara for six weeks first.' (Specific ask with a specific reason.) 'I haven't yet had to come into a room that didn't want me there.' (Names the genuine gap.) This is the answer that distinguishes a confirmed SM from a trusted-with-harder-work SM.]_

**Adisa:** That's the right answer. Let me see what I can do.

---

_The SM walked out of the room without an explicit confirmation but with two pieces of information. One: Adisa was thinking about her next role before this conversation. Two: 'that's the right answer' was the closest thing to a yes Adisa was going to give in the room. Confirmed-and-trusted-with-harder-work, in practice._

annotations.note: Self-assessment uses 'Held' instead of 'Delivered' as the first column header. This is the structural difference between the SM probation pack and the PM one. The SM's job is holding; the language of the assessment should match the job.

The two-horizon question in the pre-review 1:1 ('what does good look like now AND in a year?') is the SM-specific reframe. SMs are assessed on trajectory; the question makes trajectory the explicit subject of the conversation.

Evidence portfolio for an SM is a list of moments held, not a list of artefacts delivered. The 'what was at stake' column is the discipline that makes the invisible visible. Without it, the portfolio reads as 'I closed 12 impediments' — true but doesn't tell Adisa anything about whether you can hold a hard room.

The annotated conversation is the most valuable single piece in this pack. Read it twice. The first read teaches you the moves; the second read teaches you the reasoning behind the moves. The structure ('SM's silent thought' next to 'SM says') is the structure you should rehearse in your own head before the meeting.

common_mistakes: Self-assessment that lists ceremonies run rather than moments held. 'Ran 12 retros' tells Adisa nothing. 'Held the room when Naledi cried in week 9' tells her everything.
Pre-review 1:1 booked too late. The whole point is to learn what your reviewer needs in the formal review, in time to actually adjust your pack. Book it a week before; eight days if you can.
Evidence portfolio of impediments closed and ceremonies run. SMs who present their value this way underperform their own reviews. The value is in moments held; surface those.
Reading the conversation playbook once. Read it twice. The second read is where the annotations make sense.
Treating the formal review as a presentation. It's a conversation. The pack is so the conversation can happen; the pack itself doesn't get presented.
Answering the 'harder room' question with either 'yes please' or 'I'm not ready'. Both are wrong. The right shape is 'I'd want it, and here's the specific support I'd want to be ready for it'.
variant_patterns: Extended-probation variant: if the outcome was 'extended', the conversation playbook reshapes around the question 'what specifically would land as continued in the next 30 days?' — pulling specificity from the reviewer rather than asking 'what do I need to improve'.

First-SM-on-the-team variant (the team has never had a dedicated SM): the evidence portfolio shifts to include 'what we introduced and the team kept' (ceremonies, agreements). The probation review will partly be about whether the role itself is justified.
Non-standard probation length variant: structure unchanged. Probation Mode activates 21 days before the actual review date, whatever it is.
